label: Transmitted Enlightenment feminist critique into 19th-century liberal reform
description: Harriet Taylor Mill carried forward Wollstonecraft's demand for women's intellectual and civic emancipation, pushing beyond educational reform to demand full political suffrage and independent economic self-support.
dialecticalTension: Advances Enlightenment moral equality into concrete democratic enfranchisement and labor rights.
historicalContext: 19th-century British radical liberal and feminist thought (1832–1851).

label: Supplied utilitarian egalitarianism expanded to women's suffrage and domestic freedom
description: Working within Benthamite philosophical radicalism, Taylor Mill applied equal-consideration utilitarianism to dismantle legal coverture and patriarchal marriage.
dialecticalTension: Pushes classical utilitarianism past male-centered political reforms.
historicalContext: British Unitarian and philosophical radical circles (1830s–1850s).

label: Co-shaped On Liberty, Principles of Political Economy, and utilitarian feminism
description: John Stuart Mill explicitly credited Harriet Taylor Mill as co-author of the core ideas in On Liberty and Principles of Political Economy, and her 1851 Enfranchisement of Women laid the foundation for his Subjection of Women.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes radical feminist egalitarianism and cooperative socialism into canonical liberalism.
historicalContext: Twenty-eight-year philosophical partnership culminating in On Liberty (1859).

label: Extended rational equality to universal suffrage and economic independence
description: In The Enfranchisement of Women (1851), Taylor Mill argued that true equality requires women's full participation in political voting and paid professions rather than confining them to domesticity.
dialecticalTension: Deepens abstract equality of reason into concrete economic and political rights.
historicalContext: Published in the Westminster Review (1851) inspired by the Worcester Women's Rights Convention.
